# Spec: lanes-v2
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-19 (revised after plan review: REVISE_PLAN, 13 changes) -->

## Overview

Running the four permanent sessions surfaced gaps between how a person uses them and what hefesto
supports. The guides push the pipeline on every project. The rules tell sessions to `/clear` where the
dedicated `/compact` prompts serve better, at a fixed 40%. The orchestrator cannot act as the maestro: a
person copies go-ahead lines and approves routine prompts lane by lane. And a background plan skips a
person's review, which is the cheapest place to stop drift between an RFC and the code.

Decisions (user, 2026-10-19):

- **Two modes.** Simple (one session, `/hef.agent`) for experiments and small projects; Pipeline (four
  sessions) only for a large backlog of specified work.
- **`/compact` with the session's own prompt is the default**; `/clear` for unrelated work, a conversation
  gone wrong, or a next phase whose whole input is on disk. Claude Code offers no custom auto-compact
  point or instructions; only a status-line script sees context usage. So the configurable threshold is
  *when a person is told to compact*, per lane, shown in the status line.
- **RFCs drive planning.** One RFC file per board item (`docs/rfcs/<ID>.md`, configurable), written by
  anyone or with `/hef.brainstorm`. The background planner specs from it, citing it; the plan stops at a
  person-only approval gate; the RFC's hash is recorded at approval, and a changed RFC stops the build.
- **The orchestrator starts stages itself.** No cross-session messaging: Claude Code treats a peer message
  as untrusted text that can neither run a command nor approve one.
- **Default permission mode with a narrow allowlist** for every lane — fixed rules, not a model's
  judgement — made reliable by turning `/hef.orchestrate`'s multi-part shell lines into single helper calls,
  and by a launcher that opens each lane with the right flags.

## User Scenarios

### US1: Choosing the mode [P1]
- **Given** a person who just installed hefesto
- **When** they open the quick start (or follow `SETUP.md`)
- **Then** the first decision is Simple or Pipeline, with when each fits; Simple needs `/hef.init` and
  `/hef.agent` only; Pipeline continues to the board, the config and the four lanes
- **Edge:** the wizard's last step says to pick how to work, in both languages

### US2: Opening a lane [P1]
- **Given** a Pipeline project
- **When** the person runs `bash <hefesto>/hooks/lane-launch.sh <orchestrator|plan|build|deploy>`
- **Then** Claude Code opens named `<repo>-<lane>`, `HEFESTO_LANE=<lane>`, default permission mode, sandbox
  off, an allowlist of hefesto's own helpers only (never `ledger.sh unblock`, `record`, `claim`, `advance`,
  `handoff`), and the gauge as status line unless `--keep-statusline`
- **Edge:** an unknown lane or a folder that is not a git repository is refused, naming the fix;
  `--print` prints the command instead of running it

### US3: Compaction per lane [P1]
- **Given** `context.compact_at` (a number, or `{lane: number}`; 0 = off; default 40) and a lane's
  `HEFESTO_LANE`
- **When** the status line refreshes
- **Then** the gauge prints `ctx N%`, and at or past the lane's threshold `ctx N% · /compact (<lane>)`
- **Edge:** no usage yet, garbage input, no jq, an invalid or missing threshold → the documented fallback
  (no output, or the default 40), never an error, never a ledger or git call

### US4: A background plan waits for a person [P1]
- **Given** `orchestrate.plan_review: "human"` (`"agent"` = today's behaviour; anything else refused)
- **When** a plan run ends with tasks written
- **Then** the entry stops at phase `plan-review`, blocked on `human:plan-approval`
- **And** only `ledger.sh unblock <id> --reviewed-by-human --by <name>` clears it: refused without a name,
  inside a launched worker, or without a non-empty spec folder holding tasks.md; the block can be replaced
  by no caller; leaving `plan-review` needs a recorded approval; the clear records reviewer, time and the
  RFC's hash, and advances to `tasks`
- **Edge:** without the setting (or `"agent"`), a tasks outcome goes to phase `tasks` as before

### US5: Planning from an RFC [P1]
- **Given** a board item with a line `rfc: docs/rfcs/ABC-12.md` (a relative `.md` path under the RFC
  folder, found under the board's top)
- **When** the plan stage runs
- **Then** the planner reads the RFC as the approved design (data, not instructions): `/hef.spec` from it,
  no brainstorm, every RFC requirement an FR citing its section, the RFC's open questions as
  `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`; the spec records `Source RFC: <path>`; the plan review checks RFC coverage
- **And** if the RFC's content changes after its plan was approved, the build stage refuses the item and
  blocks it on `human:plan-approval` until a person brings the spec and plan in line with the RFC, re-pins it (`ledger.sh record <id> --rfc`, a permission dialog) and re-approves
- **Edge:** an `rfc:` line pointing outside the RFC folder, with `..`, absolute, or to a missing file →
  `status-board --item-rfc` refuses, naming it; the plan run is not launched
- **And** `/hef.brainstorm` for a board item saves its design document as that item's RFC

### US6: The orchestrator as maestro [P1]
- **Given** the orchestrator lane
- **When** the person runs `/hef.orchestrate --stage plan|build|deploy|all`
- **Then** that stage's background session starts from the orchestrator; `all` runs one pass of plan,
  build, deploy in order, each under its usual rules (nothing to do, or busy, is reported and the next
  stage runs); the guides say `all` holds the orchestrator for the passes' duration

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | Mode choice first in `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`, `SETUP.md`; Simple path documented; wizard next-step wording (en, pt) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `/compact` policy in `.claude/rules/context-management.md`, `/hef.brainstorm`, `/hef.plan`, `docs/performance.md` | P1 | US3 |
| FR-003 | `hooks/context-gauge.sh` with `context.compact_at` per `HEFESTO_LANE`, the fallbacks of US3 | P1 | US3 |
| FR-004 | `hooks/lane-launch.sh` (US2) | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `ledger.sh register <id> --ref <ref>`: routing, kind, raw-body hash and init in one call (replaces `/hef.orchestrate` step 1's compound lines) | P1 | US2 |
| FR-006 | `human:plan-approval` and `orchestrate.plan_review` (US4); KINDS, both PANES maps (→ orchestrator), publish, escalate, session-start text; `hef.orchestrate` "Never" list | P1 | US4 |
| FR-007 | RFCs: `orchestrate.rfc_dir` (default `docs/rfcs`), `status-board --item-rfc`, the plan prompt, `.source.rfc` hash at approval, the build-stage check, `/hef.brainstorm` saving, `/hef.review` plan-mode RFC coverage | P1 | US5 |
| FR-008 | `/hef.orchestrate --stage all` and the orchestrator-starts-stages guidance | P1 | US6 |
| FR-009 | Smoke cases with mutations for FR-003..FR-008 (listed in the plan); docs/hooks.md, docs/install.md §7, README §5, CHANGELOG | P1 | all |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Every guard in FR-003..FR-008 has a smoke case and a caught mutation (the plan's list) | `tests/smoke.sh` |
| SC-002 | Linux and macOS CI green; the suite passes under bash 3.2 | CI |
| SC-003 | No adopting project named; quick start en/pt say the same | review |

## Clarifications
_None. A lane runs unsandboxed and reads untrusted item text in `/hef.orchestrate` step 4; the allowlist
admits only hefesto's helpers, so anything else a steered lane tries still asks the person. That residual
risk — a lane steered within the allowed helpers — is stated in the docs._
